subject: Re: Token economics & migration approach — matching cloud benchmarks
body:
From: Dave Liu <dave.liu@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers?

Irene,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement and our platform team asked for a direct compare: Acme is evaluating three options for hosted inference (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Redwood). The ask from procurement is simple — show us a path to price parity on per-token while keeping predictable costs for the next 12 months.

Specifics: our forecast is ~12B tokens / month (steady-state) with 6–8M peak-day tokens. We need a proposal that includes commit tiers, overage rates, and any migration credits or one-time offsets you can offer to displace our OpenAI contract. Also want to understand any constraints on model variants and bursting.

Can you send a short proposal and a mutual action plan timeline?

Thanks,
Dave Liu
Principal Platform Engineer, Acme Corp

-----Original Message-----
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Dave Liu <dave.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers?

Dave — really appreciate the clarity here. High level answer: yes — we can build a displacement offer that reaches competitive per-token economics, but it requires a mix of committed volume, a short-term migration credit, and a few operational guardrails (SLO-based burst caps and model-variant pinning for consistent latency).

I attached a baseline model (pricing_model.xlsx) and a short performance summary (benchmark_summary.csv). Quick bullets: 
- Baseline per-token rates: anchored to tiered commit (see sheet "TieredRates").
- Migration: we can provide a one-time migration credit equal to up to 10% of the first 6 months' committed spend if you sign a 12-month commit and share usage telemetry during onboarding.
- Burst: support for 2x burst above committed QPS for short windows; sustained burst requires higher reserved capacity.
- Model variants: open options — we recommend pinning for production endpoints that need strict latency.

Ben/Aditya — can we propose a 3-tier commit structure (12B steady -> tier 1, 20B -> tier 2, 30B+ -> tier 3) with blended per-token pricing and a migration credit line item? Laura, what's the acceptable range on upfront credits and what strings do we need?

Irene
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: benchmark_summary.csv (CSV)

-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers?

Team — draft play: 
1) Offer a 12-month committed deal with quarterly true-ups. Tiers: 12B/mo (tier A), 18–22B/mo (tier B), 30B+/mo (tier C).
2) Per-token blended price adjusts per tier; include an "initial migration credit" equal to 8% of the first 3 months' committed spend (finance can increase if needed).
3) Include a 90-day performance warranty: if latency or availability metrics are not hit, automatic fallback to a cold model endpoint and additional credit applied.
4) Selling point: Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization + caching) projected to reduce net per-token by ~15% on Acme's typical prompt distribution. Include that in the TCO slide.

Aditya — can you draft a short MAP for technical onboarding and procurement milestones (SOW, security questionnaire, SOC2 evidence, test tokens)?

-Ben
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers?

Ben, Irene — finance constraints and risk profile: 
- Credit cap: we can commit up to 12% migration credit on a 12-month commit but that requires a minimum committed spend of $1.2M/mo. For lower commits, max credit is 6%.
- Discount floors: internal policy prohibits exceeding 40% off list per-token without CFO approval. Anything with guaranteed credits that push effective discount beyond that must be routed through revenue ops.
- Billing cadence: monthly with quarterly reconciliation. Overage rates must be ~1.15x of committed-per-token to avoid perverse incentives.
- Contract redlines: no open-ended data egress guarantees — we will offer defined export windows and an audit log SLA.

If we include any "migration rebate" it must be contingent on: shared usage telemetry during onboarding, a 60‑day ramp clause, and a 30‑day clawback window if Acme terminates early.

-Laura
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Dave Liu <dave.liu@acme.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers? (Mutual Action Plan)

Dave — attaching a short MAP and timeline. Key milestones: 
- Week 1: Execute NDA + SOW; collect SOC 2 artifact set and security questionnaire answers.
- Week 2: PoC environment (shared telemetry stream) with 50M test tokens and performance verification.
- Week 3–4: Migrate 30% traffic with monitoring; tune batching/kv-cache settings.
- Week 5: Cutover and settle committed volumes & credits.

We propose the following commercial outline (high level):
- 12-month commit: 12B tokens/mo baseline. Effective per-token after 8% migration credit: $0.0008/token (blended) for Tier A.
- Tier B (18–22B): $0.00072/token effective.
- Tier C (30B+): $0.00065/token effective + priority burst pool.

Notes: the effective per-token includes predictable cost reductions from Redwood Optimize and a migration credit applied on month 1–3 invoices. Full terms in the attached redline_terms.pdf.

Attachment: redline_terms.pdf (PDF)

-----Original Message-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dave Liu <dave.liu@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers? (Commercial ask)

Quick POV from sales leadership: 
- We should avoid an absolute price-match guarantee vs OpenAI/Anthropic. Instead offer a limited displacement package: a short-term credit + performance SLAs + a 60‑day price-protect clause (if Acme signs and within 60 days a competitor reduces price more than X%, Redwood will match the delta up to a cap).
- Emphasize operational advantages: predictable reserved capacity, per-route latency SLOs, and the Optimize-driven TCO reductions. These are differentiators vs raw per-token pricing.
- For procurement, frame credits as "migration assistance" rather than a permanent discount — lower churn risk.

Ben, please prioritize the MAP and the commercial summary; Laura, finalize the cap language and clawback. Irene, want you to lead the technical onboarding notes for the PoC.

-Vivek
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Dave Liu <dave.liu@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token economics — can Redwood match cloud tiers?

Irene/Team — appreciate the thoughtful structure. A few clarifying asks before procurement takes this to legal: 
1) Can you provide a worked example invoice for month 1 showing migration credit application and how overage would bill if we spike to 2x committed tokens for a 24‑hour window?
2) For the 60‑day price-protect, what's the exact cap percentage you would accept? Acme typically asks for up to 20% match on price drops in industry announcements.
3) Are there any model-variant restrictions that would materially change effective cost (e.g., if we switch to an XXL variant on peak days)?

If you can send a short worked invoice + updated MAP with the 60‑day cap number, we can expedite to legal.

Thanks,
Dave
Principal Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
